import re
P='docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex'
s=open(P).read()
i=s.index(r"\begin{schema}{LcReleaseClaim}")

new=r"""\begin{schema}{LcReleaseClaim}
\Delta Lifecycle \\
\Xi LcTime \\
\Xi LcRoster \\
\Xi LcKind \\
\Xi LcStarted \\
\Xi LcCorrupt \\
\Xi LcLineage \\
\Xi LcSeen \\

corigin' = \{ s? \} \ndres corigin \\

python3 - <<'E'
P='docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex'
s=open(P).read()
new=r"""\paragraph{Close-time clearing} (\fpath{cmd/ethos/mission.go}:2278--2311;
\fpath{mission/active.go}:891--955). After \field{ethos mission close} the
\emph{closing} session runs \field{ClearMissionBindings}: it clears its
active-mission claim if the claim names the closed mission, and, independently,
its delegation binding if the binding's mission is the closed one. The two
tests are separate, so a session that closes a mission other than the one it
claims can keep a binding for a mission that is not its claim. That is the
state \field{fixSupersede} exists for (C9), once \field{mission release} no
longer leaves it behind.

\begin{schema}{LcClearClosed}
\Delta Lifecycle \\
\Xi LcTime \\
\Xi LcRoster \\
\Xi LcKind \\
\Xi LcStarted \\
\Xi LcCorrupt \\
\Xi LcLineage \\
\Xi LcSeen \\
\Xi LcPending \\
\Xi LcFlight \\
\Xi LcUsed \\
\Xi LcSkeleton \\
\Xi LcOpen \\
\Xi LcVerdict \\
\Xi LcMission \\
\Xi LcSealed \\
\Xi LcPurged \\
\Xi LcLeak \\
s? : SESSIONID \\
m? : MISSIONID
\where
s? \in roster \\
s? \notin \dom stage \\
m? \notin missOpen \\
(s? \mapsto m?) \in claimed \lor (\exists d : binding \limg \{ s? \} \rimg @ (d \mapsto m?) \in dMis) \\
(s? \mapsto m?) \in claimed \implies (claimed' = \{ s? \} \ndres claimed \land corigin' = \{ s? \} \ndres corigin) \\
(s? \mapsto m?) \notin claimed \implies (claimed' = claimed \land corigin' = corigin) \\
(\exists d : binding \limg \{ s? \} \rimg @ (d \mapsto m?) \in dMis) \implies binding' = \{ s? \} \ndres binding \\
\lnot (\exists d : binding \limg \{ s? \} \rimg @ (d \mapsto m?) \in dMis) \implies binding' = binding
\end{schema}

"""
s=s.replace(r"\paragraph{Missions.} \field{LcCloseLocked}", new+r"\paragraph{Missions.} \field{LcCloseLocked}")
open(P,'w').write(s)
E

tool_input.command:
python3 - <<'E'
P='docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex'
s=open(P).read()
i=s.index(r"  \item[\textbf{C9}]")
j=s.index(r"  \item[\textbf{C10}]")
newc9=r"""  \item[\textbf{C9}] \textbf{A second propagation overwrites the binding of
    the first.} \field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton} (literal form), found only
    after C1 to C8 were amended. A completed propagation: \field{LcCfBegin}$(b,a)$;
    reconcile; \field{LcCfAlloc}$(b,d_1)$ and the four writes; \field{LcCfFinish}.
    Then the child's claim is replaced by an operator claim of another
    mission $m_2$ and $m_2$ is closed by the child's own session
    (\field{LcOperatorClaim}, \field{LcCloseLocked}, \field{LcClearClosed}):
    \field{ClearMissionBindings} clears the claim, which names $m_2$, and
    leaves the binding, which names $d_1$ of $m_1$ (the two tests are
    independent, \fpath{mission/active.go}:907--935). A second
    \field{claim-forked}: \field{LcCfBegin}$(b,a)$; reconcile (the record is
    gone); \field{LcCfAlloc}$(b,d_2)$; the writes up to
    \field{LcCfWriteBinding} (run \texttt{T3\_nosup}, nineteen steps). The
    binding now names $d_2$; $d_1$ is open, named by no record and no
    binding. \textbf{Errata (this revision).} The first statement of C9 reached
    the same state by \field{LcReleaseClaim} leaving the binding in place.
    That was a defect of the model, not of the code: \field{ethos mission
    release} clears the binding as well as the claim
    (\fpath{cmd/ethos/mission.go}:2150--2153), so after a release there is no
    binding for a second propagation to overwrite. The state is reached by
    the close-time clearing above, which is why \field{fixSupersede} is
    still needed (\texttt{T3\_nosup} counterexample, \texttt{T3\_all}
    holds). \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixSupersede}, with its scope stated
    exactly: it applies on the two reconcile paths that go on to write, that
    is \field{LcCfReconcileFresh} and \field{LcCfReconcileReuse}, whether or
    not a pending record exists, and on no other path. It closes the open
    \field{dkFork} skeleton the child's binding names when that is not the
    skeleton the call will use: on the fresh path every such skeleton, on the
    resume path the one that differs from the record's. It is never applied
    by \field{LcCfRefuse} or \field{LcCfReconcileClaimed}, whose child either
    does not write or holds a claim, and may be working under the binding. The
    earlier wording, ``a reconcile that does not resume the record'',
    contradicted the schema of \field{LcCfReconcileReuse}, which carries the
    clause; it is withdrawn.
  \item[\textbf{C11}] \textbf{\field{mission release} leaves the skeleton it
    unnames open.} \field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton}; found by reading the
    release command that C9 had modelled wrongly. After a completed
    propagation, \field{LcReleaseClaim}$(b)$ clears the claim and the binding
    and nothing closes $d_1$ (run \texttt{T2\_norel}: eleven steps). The
    skeleton is open, named by nothing, and the child that held it has no claim.
    \textbf{Amendment} \field{fixReleaseCloses}: \field{mission release} closes,
    \field{aborted}, the open \field{dkFork} skeleton owned by the session that
    its binding names, before it clears the binding, under the same locks
    as the other closes. A binding that names a Tier B skeleton is cleared
    and the skeleton is left open: it is a subagent's delegation.
  \item[\textbf{C12}] \textbf{A Tier B dispatch by a propagated child buries
    its fork skeleton.} \field{NoOrphanOpenSkeleton}; open, not amended. The
    child $b$ completes a propagation (binding $d_1$, kind \field{dkFork}) and
    then spawns a subagent against the mission: the dispatch writes
    \emph{its} binding for $b$ over $d_1$ (\fpath{pretooluse\_dispatch.go}:880--884),
    and $d_1$ is open, named by nothing (\field{LcTierBDispatch}, run
    \texttt{T2\_all} with \field{assumeNoTierBOverFork} off). No close in the
    design can find $d_1$ afterwards, since every close is by name. The
    constant \field{assumeNoTierBOverFork} excludes the dispatch from a session
    whose binding names an open fork skeleton, so that the other invariants
    can be checked; it is an assumption of the verification and not a fix.
    The options are listed in \S\ref{sec:lc-consequences}; the choice belongs
    to the leader.
"""
s=s[:i]+newc9+s[j:]
# C10 should precede C11/C12: move C10 block after C9? order: C9, C11, C12, C10 -> fix by renaming: swap labels
open(P,'w').write(s)
E
grep -n "item\[\\\\textbf{C1[012]" docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex
